# name: # System groups with no users, declared by upstream sysusers.d (systemd
# basic.conf) and required complete for deterministic databases. utmp
# tracks login-accounting groups; empower is upstream systemd's
# administrator-group companion. Neither is referenced by anything in
# Saphira today, but a missing declared group is an image-build error,
# not a notice, so they are seeded rather than skipped. Fixed low IDs
# continuing the classic block - deliberately NOT Egg's historical
# 998/999 local assignments, which live in the local/admin range no
# package or seed may allocate from.
# Device-owner groups referenced by shipped udev rules and tmpfiles
# fragments (no corresponding users: purely device ownership). Without
# them every boot logs "Unknown group" and the nodes fall back to the
# wrong group - notably /dev/rtc0 (clock) and /dev/kvm (kvm). IDs live
# in 157-163: the 100-123 service block is taken, 124/126/132 are owned
# by published repo packages (hostapd, breathgslb, qmail - the repo
# gate gives published packages no reason to move, so the seed
# vacates), 127-131 and 144-145 are systemd sysusers pins, and the
# rest below 157 is repo-claimed. Stay far below the human range.
# plugdev sits outside the block at the first free ID above the
# claimed range (177): 164 was taken by the published keystone
# service identity (claimed 2026-10-18, before this seed row
# existed), and the same vacate rule applies - udev rules reference
# the GROUP NAME (libjaylink: GROUP="plugdev"), never the number,
# so the move is free and J-Link membership keeps working.
# Backfill 2026-10-27 (GO-2): every packaged identity published in
# hatched or declared by a fragment, recorded verbatim. The 84 rows
# above stay byte-identical. This file is the sole identity mint:
# fragments declare requirements, makepkg refuses any declaration
# that does not match a row here, and rows are only ever appended,
# never modified or removed. init column: empty means both inits
# (identical databases under OpenRC and systemd); 'systemd' marks
# systemd-daemon identities. No other value exists.
